advances: Attained fixed-projection bounded-facet minimum with all positive fibers. The stress concerns the assigned whole-plane cap circuits and the restricted individual-fan support chart. The base barycenter can be nonintegral. A per-group depth payment is a separate inequality.

proof:
The actual critical circuit theorem 755cb08c379113cc supplies these circuits at the positive compatible fibers. At a mark through which all its cap planes pass, continuous balance gives $h_i=A_i\cdot z_i$. Thus on the entire plane over $p$ the positively weighted sum of cap margins is $A_i\cdot p-h_i$, and a nonnegative sum guarantees coverage by the closed caps. Apply the selection part of 0354aa9a30918591. In the present lattice-convex case at most $2^n$ projected halfspaces suffice to cover $P$: replace the strict complements by closed halfspaces with identical traces on finite $P$, include $\operatorname{conv}P$, and apply [Doignon's lattice Helly theorem](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01949705). A selected group originating at a nondeep site cannot cover the plane of a deepest site, because at the latter's maximizing mark this would give a containing cap of mass less than $\beta M$. Retain the deepest-origin groups from the selection and add the original local group at each nondeep site. Fix any assignment as stated.

The reference family and its caps are feasible for the assigned coverage constraints and for the common upper cap budget $\beta M$. The fixed positive weights and continuous balance make the assigned coverage implication valid after every feasible change in $(v,b)$, even with simultaneous fiber shape changes. If a competitor in the same bounded-facet class had volume $M'>M$, each actual point would lie in a cap of mass at most $\beta M$ and its normalized depth would be at most $\beta M/M'<\beta$. If the class is formulated with unit volume at the specified interior lattice base, the positive nearby competitor there may be scaled to that volume by common continuous dilation, preserving normalized depth and facet counts. Thus the reference is a local volume maximum subject to the joint budgets and assigned coverage, in the facet-preserving chart.

Use the restricted support chart and common erosion from the proof of b380e7ea668df13d. For each fiber take the stable normal fan of its sufficiently small positive inner parallel bodies. On a common simplicial refinement require the fiber's support function to be linear on its own such fan. The resulting chart is a finite linear subspace with the homogeneous convex-support and compatibility inequalities of the fixed-fan construction used there. Its active rows, denoted $A_0$, give the exact radial cone $A_0\dot h\ge0$. The small-erosion fans have exactly the original facet normals as rays, so these changes stay in the original facet bound, and small feasible steps retain positive fibers. At each original facet its normal is fixed and its outward speed is $\dot h_z(n_F)$ for unit normal $n_F$. Adding the free variables $(\dot v,\dot b)$ and the active linear inequalities $DC_{ip}\ge0$ gives the exact joint radial cone, because the inactive rows have strict slack. The common erosion $e$ in this chart has outward speed $-1$ on each original facet and $\dot v=\dot b=0$, so it belongs to the joint radial cone and leaves every coverage row unchanged. The objective's first derivative is the linear facet flux $DM=\sum_{z,F}|F|\dot h_z(n_F)$.

For each cap apply the strip proof of 7a5ea4f8a4c5094c one fiber at a time with one owner per facet and fixed continuous normals. For a nonunit $u_{ij}$ divide the cap margin and its speed by $\|u_{ij}\|$ before using this formula. On a coincident facet write $a=\dot h_z(n_F)$ and $k=(\dot v_{ij}\cdot z-\dot b_{ij})/\|u_{ij}\|$. The forward derivative density is $\min(a,k)$ when the body lies inside the cap and $\max(a+k,0)$ when it lies outside. The noncoincident terms are the strict-inside facet flux and the proper-section flux in the statement. Since both speeds are constant on each coincident facet, the derivative on any direction is one of a finite list of linear covectors obtained by choosing its branches at each facet. A convex combination of the branch covectors has exactly the stated consistent coefficients: inside take a convex combination of $a$ and $k$, and outside one of $a+k$ and zero. In particular a single choice for each facet fixes its body and cap contributions jointly.

Every active cap has positive mass $\beta M$. On some fiber its affine margin has positive maximum, attained at a vertex. A relatively open patch of an incident facet lies strictly inside that cap and has positive area. It contributes strictly negatively on the erosion direction to every branch covector. Every other term on that direction is nonpositive, since the facet speeds are $-1$ and the cap margin speed is zero. Hence all branches of every active cap decrease strictly on $e$.

Suppose a joint radial direction increased the linear objective and paired nonpositively with every active cap branch. Adding a sufficiently small positive multiple of $e$ would retain objective gain and radial feasibility and make every active branch strictly negative. A small positive radial step would then increase actual volume and strictly decrease every active cap mass. The inactive budgets persist by continuity. This contradicts volume maximality. The finite polyhedral cone alternative therefore writes
$$
DM=\sum_{i,j}\lambda_{ij}L_{ij}
-\sum_{i,p}\eta_{ip}DC_{ip}-\gamma^{\mathsf T}A_0
$$
on the joint chart, with nonnegative coefficients supported on active rows. Indeed, the set where all active cap branches are nonpositive and all radial rows are nonnegative is contained in $\{DM\le0\}$, so $DM$ lies in its polar cone generated by the active cap branches and the negatives of the active radial rows. Group each cap's branch coefficients into a nonnegative multiplier and a single convexified cap covector $L_{ij}$ of the stated form. A cap with zero multiplier can use any allowed branch allocation. This gives objective coefficient one.

Only $L_{ij}$ and its own coverage rows depend on the free offset $b_{ij}$. In that coordinate the cap coefficient is $-S_{ij}$ and each relevant coverage coefficient is $-\rho_{ij}$. In the free base coefficient coordinate $v_{ij}$ they are $\sum_zs_{ijz}z$ and $\rho_{ij}p$. Evaluating the identity yields the two displayed balance equations. Any deepest-origin cap properly cuts its positive anchor fiber through an interior maximizing point, so $S_{ij}>0$ irrespective of supporting-facet allocations elsewhere. A slack group has $\lambda_{ij}=0$ and the threshold balance gives $t_i=0$, forcing every $\eta_{ip}=0$. In a deepest-origin group the threshold balance and $S_{ij}>0$ make $t_i>0$ equivalent to all its cap multipliers being positive. Dividing the two balances gives the common barycenter for a stressed group. It is an average of assigned deepest bases and all terms of positive weight have $C_{ip}=0$, so $A_i\cdot\bar z_i=h_i$. Therefore the signed offset sum for that group is $t_i\sum_j\rho_{ij}(b_{ij}-v_{ij}\cdot\bar z_i)=0$. It is also zero for an unstressed group.

Finally evaluate the stress on joint dilation of the continuous bodies and all $(v_{ij},b_{ij})$ by the same factor, with $u_{ij}$ fixed. The active compatibility and coverage rows vanish by homogeneity. Every branch equals the actual cap derivative on this direction. At an inside coincidence the cap and body planes move at the same speed, giving $a=k$; at an outside coincidence they give $a+k=0$. The other terms are ordinary cap derivatives. Each cap mass and total mass scale by the $d$th power of the factor. Thus $dM=\sum_{i,j}\lambda_{ij}d\mu(H_{ij})$. The positive multipliers are on cap masses $\beta M$, proving $\sum_{i,j}\lambda_{ij}=1/\beta$. Substituting the threshold balances gives the last formula.

statement:
Fix $n,d\ge1$, a finite full-rank lattice-convex $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ with an interior lattice point, and a compatible family $(K_z)_{z\in P}$ of positive $d$-dimensional polytopes attaining the minimum normalized maximal closed-halfspace depth $\beta>0$ in the fixed-$P$ bounded-facet class of b380e7ea668df13d. Write $M=\sum_z|K_z|$. A base is deepest if its restricted maximal normalized depth equals $\beta$.

Choose at each base $z_i$ an actual positive critical cap circuit through an interior maximizing mark, with cap margins $v_{ij}\cdot z+u_{ij}\cdot x-b_{ij}$, $u_{ij}\ne0$, and positive weights $\rho_{ij}$ with $\sum_j\rho_{ij}=1$, $\sum_j\rho_{ij}u_{ij}=0$. Every cap in a circuit has the restricted maximal raw depth at its origin as its mass. Put $A_i=\sum_j\rho_{ij}v_{ij}$ and $h_i=\sum_j\rho_{ij}b_{ij}=A_i\cdot z_i$. Select at most $2^n$ deepest-origin groups whose projected halfspaces $\{p:A_i\cdot p\ge h_i\}$ cover the deepest bases, and assign each deepest base to one of these covering groups. Such a selection exists. Assign every nondeep base to its own additional local circuit, whose caps have mass strictly below $\beta M$.

In the compatible support chart linear on each fiber's own small-erosion normal fan, allow the base coefficients and offsets of every selected cap occurrence to vary freely and keep $u_{ij},\rho_{ij}$ fixed. For every assigned pair $(i,p)$ impose $C_{ip}=\sum_j\rho_{ij}(v_{ij}\cdot p-b_{ij})\ge0$. There is an objective-one stress with nonnegative active-cap multipliers $\lambda_{ij}$, nonnegative active-coverage multipliers $\eta_{ip}$, and nonnegative multipliers of the active support and compatibility rows. Its cap covectors use consistent facet and coarea allocations. Specifically, a facet portion strictly inside a cap contributes its area times its outward support speed, and a proper cap section contributes its area divided by $\|u_{ij}\|$ times the cap margin speed $\dot v_{ij}\cdot z-\dot b_{ij}$. At a coincident facet of area $|F|$, one $\theta\in[0,1]$ supplies the facet coefficient $\theta|F|$ and the cap-margin coefficient $(1-\theta)|F|/\|u_{ij}\|$ when the body lies inside, or $\theta|F|/\|u_{ij}\|$ when it lies outside. Strictly empty and strictly full traces, and lower-dimensional supporting contacts, have zero coarea. Use counting measure for $d=1$.

Let $s_{ijz}$ be the resulting effective coarea coefficient in fiber $z$, $S_{ij}=\sum_zs_{ijz}$, and $t_i=\sum_{p\ {\rm assigned\ to}\ i}\eta_{ip}$. The same multipliers and allocations satisfy
$$
\lambda_{ij}S_{ij}=\rho_{ij}t_i,\qquad
\lambda_{ij}\sum_zs_{ijz}z=\rho_{ij}\sum_{p\ {\rm assigned\ to}\ i}\eta_{ip}p .
$$
Each $S_{ij}$ is positive in a deepest-origin group. If $t_i>0$, that group is selected from a deepest origin, each $\lambda_{ij}=t_i\rho_{ij}/S_{ij}>0$, and every cap's section-base barycenter equals
$$
\bar z_i=\frac{\sum_zs_{ijz}z}{S_{ij}}
=\frac{\sum_{p\ {\rm assigned\ to}\ i}\eta_{ip}p}{t_i},
\qquad A_i\cdot\bar z_i=h_i .
$$
Thus $\bar z_i$ lies in the convex hull of its assigned globally deepest bases. Every group with $t_i=0$ has zero cap and coverage stress. The signed offsets cancel groupwise, and the full normalization is
$$
\sum_{j,z}\lambda_{ij}(b_{ij}-v_{ij}\cdot z)s_{ijz}=0
\quad\text{for every }i,\qquad
\sum_{i,j}\lambda_{ij}=\frac1\beta
=\sum_{i:t_i>0}t_i\sum_j\frac{\rho_{ij}}{S_{ij}}.
$$
title: Normalized joint stress for selected critical cap groups in the bounded-facet class
